source.title: On the Learning Dynamics of Two-layer Linear Networks with Label Noise SGD
source.authors: Tong-Cheng Zhang; Zhan-Peng Zhou; Mingze Wang; Andi Han; Wei Huang; Taiji Suzuki; Jun-Chi Yan

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. It includes figures as descriptions but no recoverable plotted values.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests label-noise training dynamics in a two-layer linear network and WideResNets on a small CIFAR-10 subset, a setting related to but outside the claim versions' core classification-error outcomes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that a ResNet-18 trained on CIFAR-10 with label-noise SGD improves test accuracy and pruning performance. These results concern generalization and sparsity, not training classification error, so they do not form rows for the listed versions. Its reported WideResNet experiments concern loss trajectories and first-layer weight norms; the plotted values are figure-only and the text does not report numerical outcomes. The synthetic experiments describe norm reduction, alignment and convergence, but use a linear regression model and do not report classification error.
record.test_reason: The study's own results concern noise-induced feature learning, weight norms, alignment, regression convergence, test accuracy and pruning. None measures a listed version's training classification error, spurious-minimum frequency, depth degradation, initialization comparison, stability-threshold dynamics or normalization advantage.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' interpretation: label noise induces second-layer oscillation and first-layer norm reduction, promoting a transition from lazy to rich dynamics, with similar empirical behavior under SAM. Qualify the convergence statement: the formal Phase II alignment and convergence results switch to noiseless gradient descent and assume small weights and, for convergence, perfect alignment. Extending the theory to nonlinear networks and classification remains future work.
record.recipe_differences: Studies label-noise SGD in an over-parameterized two-layer linear regression network and rich-regime behavior in WideResNets; the reported outcomes focus on dynamics, generalization and sparsity rather than training classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: Label-noise probability varies in the ResNet-18 CIFAR-10 experiment; alternating noisy and noiseless SGD changes when first-layer norm reduction occurs. No numerical values are provided in the text for these figure-based comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 1 reports about 1.5 percentage points higher CIFAR-10 test accuracy with label-noise SGD across flipping probabilities 0.05, 0.1 and 0.2, plus better accuracy at matched pruning levels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Injected label noise can improve ResNet-18 generalization and pruning performance under the tested recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.5 and Figure 3 report that noisy-label training of WideResNets on 64 CIFAR-10 images departs from linearized-model trajectories and reduces first-layer weight norms.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Injected label noise can induce feature-learning dynamics in the tested WideResNet setting.

fits_no_version.finding: The two-layer linear regression analysis and experiments describe initial norm reduction followed by alignment; the formal Phase II results use noiseless gradient descent and conditional assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label noise can drive departure from lazy dynamics, with subsequent conditional alignment and convergence under gradient descent.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5 reports analogous norm-reduction and alignment dynamics for SAM in synthetic experiments and departure from linearized trajectories in WideResNets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM can induce feature-learning dynamics in the tested synthetic and CIFAR-10 subset settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix E reports that first-layer norm reduction occurs during noisy intervals and stops during noiseless intervals when training alternates every 5,000 steps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Injected label noise controls norm-reduction dynamics in the tested two-layer linear network.

record.problems: Relevant real-world plots do not provide extractable numeric values in the supplied text. The real-world CIFAR-10 experiment uses a random subset of 64 images for the WideResNet analysis, and the authors state that extending their theory to classification remains open.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows: the reported results measure test accuracy, pruning performance, loss trajectories, weight norms and alignment, not any version's named training-error, depth, initialization, learning-rate or normalization outcome.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels, and its dependence on size or training recipe.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks and their reduction with extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training error in plain networks and prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient preservation, and comparative training speed or trainable depth.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature evolution relative to the stability threshold, and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparison with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Change the reader's tests/T3 classification to discusses/T6. Empty qualifying rows and verdicts are appropriate. Numerical results are not entirely absent from the text: Figure 1 explicitly reports an approximately 1.5 percentage point test-accuracy improvement, which bears on none of V1–V6.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 or corrupted/random labels; does not compare model size, early stopping or regularized recipes on that outcome.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment, spurious minima rate, or student-width comparison.
No plain-versus-residual depth comparison on training error. The WideResNet experiment examines label-noise effects on training trajectories, not the stated depth and shortcut outcome.
No comparison of initialization methods on learning speed or trainable depth.
No above-stability learning-rate sweep, curvature threshold, or divergence comparison.
No batch-normalization comparison on accuracy speed or learning-rate tolerance, and no Fixup experiment.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
